name: Kolaiah
overview: Kolaiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Maaseiah. His mention in Scripture is brief and specific, with no additional personal notes recorded. His identity is primarily grounded in his familial connection within the Benjaminite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Kolaiah means "y-h-v-h’s voice," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the voice or message of the LORD. This proper name is noted in Nehemiah 11:7 and carries a meaning that connects the individual to God's communication.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Kolaiah was the son of Maaseiah. It is also inferred that Pedaiah was his father, establishing a generational link within his family. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Kolaiah's significance in the biblical narrative is closely tied to his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:7. His identification as the son of Maaseiah situates him within the post-exilic community, emphasizing the restoration of Israel's tribes and families. Though his role is not elaborated upon, his mention contributes to the broader biblical record of God's faithfulness in preserving His people through their lineage.
